About this site

This site describes the Current Population Survey, Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC), published by U.S. Census Bureau (for the Bureau of Labor Statistics). It is generated from the repository pdt-cps-asec, which holds metadata built from the publisher's documentation: each variable's label, question text, codes and missing codes, and availability, with corrections and links between releases. Each fact says where it came from.

What it isn't

  • It isn't the publisher's site, and the publisher hasn't reviewed it. The publisher's own page for the dataset is https://www.census.gov/data/datasets/time-series/demo/cps/cps-asec.html. Where this site and the publisher's documentation differ, the publisher's documentation is the source; the differences this repository knows of are listed as corrections.
  • It doesn't hold the data. The data come from the publisher, or from this repository's data release when the terms allow; see Getting the data.
  • It makes no analysis decisions: which answers count as agreement, which weights or cases to use, or how to recode. Those belong to the projects that use the data.

What they say
Allen Downey decided on 2026-11-19 that data, documentation and metadata ship and that LLM processing is allowed, with a Census Bureau credit as the notice. Users must still not try to identify any person or household. What the sources say: the public-use files are federal works (17 U.S.C. 105), and the ASEC pages state no restriction on use or redistribution. Census's terms for its data API (https://www.census.gov/data/developers/about/terms-of-service.html) carry the Title 13 obligations: don't use the data to identify any person or household, don't link it with other data to identify anyone, and report an inadvertent identification. Citation: https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html.

PublicDataToolkit

The library and the standard that build this site: https://github.com/AllenDowney/PublicDataToolkit. This site was generated by version 0.2.0.

Reporting an error

  • In the publisher's documentation (a wrong label, a missing code, question text that belongs to another item): open an issue at the issue tracker of the repository pdt-cps-asec, with where you found it. This repository records such errors as corrections, with the evidence, and keeps the publisher's original; it also says whether the error was reported to the publisher.
  • In this repository's records (a wrong link, a code classified wrongly, a variable left out): open an issue at the issue tracker of the repository pdt-cps-asec.
  • To the publisher: U.S. Census Bureau (for the Bureau of Labor Statistics).
